conclusion: The network port is faithful: all module boundaries match fp32 at r>=0.9997.

int8 vs fp32 end-to-end structural agreement is step-count dependent. On the hardest target (no MSA), 20 steps gives 3.19 A / lDDT 0.685 (fails gate) but 50 steps gives 0.64 A / lDDT 0.977 (passes) -- few-step Euler corrections are large so per-step int8 error has high leverage; finer integration removes it.
int8 (group-64, 8-bit) is viable end-to-end at production step counts; fp16 is not required for structural fidelity.
method: int8-MLX vs fp32-PyTorch. Module-boundary Pearson r vs make-fixtures; end-to-end all-atom RMSD/lDDT over resolved atoms from reverse diffusion driven by identical injected noise + identity augmentation on both backends (Kabsch-aligned).
